core_thesis: Fear disguises itself as common sense, building walls out of old failures and invented worries — and the only way past it is to recognize the mask and act anyway.
narrative_strategy: Carry the abstract lesson on one concrete moment: a man frozen over a finished resignation letter. Move chronologically through the four story pages — hesitation, the built-but-unclaimed business, escalating panic, then the reveal that the dread has no logic — and use the text-only reflection page to turn the insight outward to the viewer in a single closing question.
hook: Mark's finger hovered over the delete key. The resignation letter was already written.
narration_script: Mark's finger hovered over the delete key. The resignation letter was already written. Six months of nights and weekends had built his freelance business. The clients were lined up. The cash was waiting. But suddenly, that boring desk job felt like a warm blanket. Then the panic got louder. A shaky economy. That one time he failed a college project. His brain building a wall between him and his bold goal. Then he saw it. The dread lacked logic. It was simply fear wearing a mask. The ego hates change, so it feeds you doubt. He closed his eyes, took a breath, and clicked send. What has your fear disguised as common sense?

voice_direction.persona: Mature, composed narrator speaking close to the microphone — steady, thoughtful, quietly intense, like someone recounting something they have lived through
delivery_notes: Open low and unhurried; let the first two sentences sit in tension rather than selling them
Clip the panic fragments slightly shorter and tighter to simulate escalating thought
Drop volume, not speed, on 'It was simply fear wearing a mask' — this is the turn
Soften and slow the final line; ask the question genuinely, do not push it
pause_after_phrases: The resignation letter was already written.
That one time he failed a college project.
It was simply fear wearing a mask.

story_arc.opening_tension: A man sits over a finished resignation letter he cannot send, his finger poised on delete.
story_arc.human_or_concrete_story: Mark spent six months of nights and weekends building a freelance business with clients lined up and cash waiting, yet his dull, secure desk job suddenly felt like a warm blanket.
story_arc.reversal_or_reveal: The dread he mistook for judgment had no logic in it — it was simply fear wearing a mask, and he sent the letter anyway.
story_arc.principle_explanation: The ego hates change, so it feeds you doubt, building walls out of past mistakes and fake worries and disguising panic as plain common sense.
story_arc.viewer_reflection: The viewer is asked to locate the place where their own fear is currently masquerading as sensible caution.

source_integrity_notes: All five supplied assets belong to one continuous four-page story plus a text-only reflection page; narration follows page order 1-4 then the reflection, which is the meaning-derived order rather than any assumed manifest order.
The header UI text 'The False Logic of Fear' repeats on all four story pages; treated as a single title, not as repeated content.

Asset img_00daa58a9bb0 flags that the illustrated figure's hair and features differ from page 1, so it may not depict the same character. The narration uses only 'he' in that section, matching the source text's own pronoun, and never re-asserts that the figure is Mark.

Asset img_b54ab1e561ef has no title or header and its link to the story is inferred from theme. It is used only for the generalized principle and the closing reflection, both of which are verbatim-supported by its own text ('disguises this panic as plain common sense').

Icon meanings in the thought bubbles (clock, crossed-out target, fortress, gear) and the ambiguity of whether the shard wall is building or shattering are interpretive, so no narration claim rests on them — only on written body text.
The page-1 quotation "I just don't think I'm ready" was dropped for length; no quoted material is paraphrased as if it were verbatim.
No outside facts, statistics, or names were added; every claim traces to a supplied body-text block.
